haiku-low.q1: They see the same generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request gets the same generic message, but no link row is created and no email is sent. The older live link stays valid.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes and only once. Using it, or issuing a newer link for the account, ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays usable. The token is untouched, so the user can retry with a valid password until the link expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. The reset deletes all session rows, including the current device. The user is redirected to /login and must log in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told; the link stays valid until expiry or replacement, and they can re-request.
haiku-low.q7: The raw 32-byte token is generated in memory and placed only in the emailed link and the queue job. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database.
haiku-low.q8: The server computes sha256(token) and looks up the password_resets row by token_hash. It is valid only if the row exists, consumed_at is null, and expires_at is in the future.
haiku-low.q9: It is the count of password_resets rows for the account created in the last hour, with no separate counter. Rows age out of the count after an hour; rows are pruned after about a day.
haiku-low.q10: Earlier unused links are invalidated by setting consumed_at to now, inside the same transaction as the new insert, only after the rate limit check passes.
haiku-low.q11: Password update, token burn (consumed_at) and deletion of all sessions happen together in one transaction. The password-changed email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The reset row is locked with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the transaction, so the second submission waits. The first commit wins; the second sees consumed_at and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same generic 200: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored and nothing is queued or sent.
sonnet.q2: Over the limit of 3 per rolling hour: the transaction rolls back, no new link, no email, the older live link stays live. The user still gets the same generic 200 message.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from issue, single use. Sooner ends: being used (consumed_at set), or being replaced by a newer link (consumed_at set when a new link is issued).
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still usable until it expires. The user gets a 422 (too short or breached, with a reason); the token is untouched and they can retry.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's session rows are deleted, so every device is logged out, including the one that did the reset. The user is redirected to /login and logs in with the new password; there is no auto-login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure (the password_resets id, not the job body) and drops the job. Nobody is notified. The user still saw the generic message, and the link stays valid until it expires or is replaced. The user can re-request, within the 3/hour limit.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the token (32 random bytes) and keeps it only in memory. It stores only the SHA-256 hash. It builds the link from the configured client base URL and the token, puts {to, link} on the email queue, and the worker sends that link in the email.
sonnet.q8: The page loads and reads the token from the URL, then asks the API to check it. The API computes h = sha256(T) and selects the password_resets row WHERE token_hash=h. It is invalid if the row is missing, consumed_at is set, or expires_at <= now(). Otherwise it is valid. The client shows the expired page for invalid and the new-password form for valid.
sonnet.q9: There is no separate counter. The count is of password_resets rows for the user with created_at in the last hour (served by the (user_id, created_at) index). Rows drop out of the count as they pass one hour old (rolling window). A periodic job prunes rows older than about a day.
sonnet.q10: Inside the request transaction, after the rate-limit check passes and before inserting the new row, the earlier unused links (consumed_at IS NULL) for that user are updated with consumed_at=now(). The new row is then inserted and the transaction commits. If the request is over the limit, nothing is changed.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: update the user's password hash, set consumed_at on the reset row, and delete all of the user's sessions. The "your password was changed" email is enqueued only after COMMIT, so a queue problem never rolls back the reset.
sonnet.q12: The POST transaction does SELECT of the reset row FOR UPDATE, a row lock. The first transaction commits and sets consumed_at. The second waits for the lock, then sees consumed_at set and gets the expired page. The first commit wins.
